This site serves files that were written by other people. This page lists them,
the licence each one is distributed under, where that statement comes from, and
where the matching source can be found. The licence texts are in the
`LICENSES/` folder of this site (27 text files, linked below file by file) and in
the repository's `site/LICENSES/` folder (the same files; the repository copy
becomes visible on the `main` branch once this page is merged). The page describes
what is provided. It is not legal advice and does not claim that every condition
of every licence has been checked.

The native board bundle additionally carries its own
[licence inventory](native/boards/mathjax/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md), original
licence files and [source provenance](native/board-mathjax.json). Those files
are additional to the 27 texts above.

Everything below was checked on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 against the files
deployed on this site; the runtime section was updated on 2026-10-26, when the
site switched to the runtime release `runtime-v3`. Older preview copies of
research branches under `previews/research/` (`2026-10-native-stack` and
`2026-10-runtime-feasibility`), where still present, serve the earlier runtime
copied from <https://maxima-on-wasm.pages.dev/>;
[the previous version of this page](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/blob/64d02c43d839ac6e8f9fb686b7c618f8a292901f/site/licenses.qmd)
describes that runtime, gnuplot included. "Evidence" means a notice inside a shipped file, a licence file in the
upstream source tree at the stated version, or both. Where neither could be
found the entry says so.

## Maxima and ECL runtime

The Maxima runtime in `maxima-runtime/` is the CTM project's release
[`runtime-v3`](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/releases/tag/runtime-v3):
Marius Gerbershagen's Emscripten port of Maxima running on ECL
(<https://gitlab.com/mgerbershagen/maxima>, the build first deployed at
<https://maxima-on-wasm.pages.dev/>), rebuilt by this project from exact,
hash-pinned sources in
[this run](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/actions/runs/40278667994)
(commit `285f8882`, compiler profile `ecl-oz-maxima-oz`).

- **Corresponding source.** The release asset
  [`maxima-runtime-v3-sources.tar.gz`](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/releases/download/runtime-v3/maxima-runtime-v3-sources.tar.gz)
  holds the exact source archives (Maxima `813903d33`, ECL `e4bdb2e5`,
  Emscripten and emsdk 4.0.10), the build recipe and the source manifest with
  every archive's SHA-256. The runtime archive
  [`maxima-runtime-v3.tar.gz`](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/releases/download/runtime-v3/maxima-runtime-v3.tar.gz)
  carries the same licence texts and the build's notices. Both are published
  beside each other for as long as the release exists.
- The site build downloads the release, checks the release record
  (`maxima-runtime-v3.json`, SHA-256 `c508649d…692c`, pinned in the repository's
  `runtime/release.json`), the archive and every runtime file against their
  hashes, and serves the files unchanged. Each file's SHA-256 is recorded in
  [`runtime-assets.json`](runtime-assets.json).
  [`runtime-preload.json`](maxima-runtime/runtime-preload.json) is assembled by
  this project from the same files (their bytes, base64-encoded) so that they
  load in one request.
- The build omits plotting: gnuplot (`libgnuplot.so`) and `maxima-plot.fas` are
  not built and not served. An authored plot gets a build diagnostic instead.
- **Modified ECL source.** The WebAssembly build of ECL carries one declared
  change by the CTM project: in `src/c/alloc_2.d`, eight root-scanning calls in
  `ecl_mark_env` and `stacks_scanner` use the collector's `GC_push_all_eager`
  instead of `GC_push_all`/`GC_push_conditional`. The exact patch, the original
  and derived file hashes and a dated comment in the changed file are in the
  release's sources archive (`source-overlays/`); the native build host uses
  unchanged ECL. ECL's licence (LGPL-2.1-or-later) and original notices apply to
  the modified file.

### Notes on the runtime {#runtime-notes}

#### Maxima {#maxima}

- Maxima's `COPYING` consists of a preface about the U.S. Department of Energy
  and the text of the GNU GPL version 2; the whole file is in
  [`LICENSES/Maxima-COPYING.txt`](LICENSES/Maxima-COPYING.txt). It was read at
  Maxima's `branch-5_49-base` tag
  (`cce856a60952c971e6f3604706335455c9a46fca`) in a GitHub mirror of Maxima's
  repository, <https://github.com/rtoy/maxima>. The shipped commit
  (`813903d33`, from the version string) is not in that mirror, so it is
  presumably on the port branch; it could not be inspected here. The version
  string means 90 commits after the 5.49 branch point of December 2025.
- The `COPYING` file does not say "or later". Most Maxima core source files
  carry only a copyright line and no licence text. Whether a given core file is
  "GPL-2.0-only" or "GPL-2.0-or-later" is therefore not stated in the files
  examined. GitLab's page for `COPYING` on the port branch (read on 2026-10-22) labels
  the project "GNU General Public License v2.0 or later".
- `maxima.wasm` contains the paths of 156 files of the port's `src/` and
  `share/utils/` trees (for example `src/mlisp.lisp`). Comparing those with the
  `branch-5_49-base` tag, these files carry notices other than the project
  licence:
  - `intl.lisp`: copyright 1999-2010 Paul Foley, an MIT-style permission notice.
    The notice from the header of that file is reproduced verbatim in
    [`LICENSES/Maxima-intl.lisp-notice.txt`](LICENSES/Maxima-intl.lisp-notice.txt)
    (no SPDX identifier assigned here).
  - `getopt.lisp`: copyright 2003 Kevin M. Rosenberg. The file's licence is
    Maxima's `LICENSES/getopt-license.txt` (three-clause BSD terms), reproduced
    unchanged in
    [`LICENSES/Maxima-getopt-license.txt`](LICENSES/Maxima-getopt-license.txt).
  - `maxmin.lisp`, `nummod.lisp`: Lisp Lesser GNU Public License (LLGPL: Franz's
    preamble, [`LICENSES/LLGPL.txt`](LICENSES/LLGPL.txt), plus the GNU Library
    General Public License version 2 or later,
    [`LICENSES/LGPL-2.0-or-later.txt`](LICENSES/LGPL-2.0-or-later.txt)). The share
    file `mring.lisp` has the same notice (see the share table).
  - `rand-mt19937.lisp`: derived from public-domain CMUCL code and the
    Mersenne Twister, noted as placed in the public domain.
  - `numerical/f2cl-lib.lisp`: header "Copyright (c) University of Waikato,
    Hamilton, New Zeland 1992-95 - all rights reserved"; no licence text.
  - `pregexp.lisp` (Dorai Sitaram): no licence text in the file.
  - `numerical/slatec.lisp`, and the contents of `maxima-slatec.fas` and
    `maxima-quadpack.fas`: Lisp translated by f2cl from the Fortran of the SLATEC
    library (which includes QUADPACK), obtained from netlib, according to
    Maxima's `src/numerical/slatec/README`. The licence status of the Fortran
    originals is not stated there and was not determined here.
- The nine `maxima-*.fas` files are compiled Maxima modules. They contain
  Maxima's symbol names and no licence text of their own.

`maxima-runtime/share/maxima/branch_5_49_base_90_g813903d33/share/` on this site,

#### ECL, GMP and the garbage collector {#ecl}

- `libecl.so` contains the strings `26.3.27` and the source id shown in the
  table, and the banner "Copyright (C) 1984 Taiichi Yuasa and Masami Hagiya,
  1993 Giuseppe Attardi, 2013 Juan J. Garcia-Ripoll, 2018 Daniel Kochmanski,
  2024 Daniel Kochmanski and Marius Gerbershagen ... ECL is free software, and you
  are welcome to redistribute it under certain conditions". The licence itself is
  in the ECL source tree: `LICENSE` at tag 26.3.27 says LGPL version 2.1 or later
  ([ECL's LICENSE](LICENSES/ECL-LICENSE.txt)). The source id in the binary
  was not found in the GitHub mirror (it may be a commit of the port's author), so
  the tag was used.
- ECL's `LICENSE` excludes from the LGPL the files `src/lsp/loop.lsp`,
  `src/lsp/pprint.lsp` and `src/lsp/format.lsp`, and the directories `contrib/`
  and `examples/`. Parts of the following are present in `libecl.so`:
  - LOOP (`src/lsp/loop.lsp`, "Symbolic's LOOP macro"): the file's strings and
    internal names (for example `LOOP-ACROSS-LIST`, `LOOP-EMIT-FINAL-VALUE`,
    `loop-minimax`) are in the binary. The file carries permission notices of the
    Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1986) and Symbolics, Inc. (1989-1992)
    that ask for the notice to appear in copies and in supporting documentation.
    The notice is reproduced verbatim from ECL 26.3.27 in
    [`LICENSES/ECL-loop.lsp-notice.txt`](LICENSES/ECL-loop.lsp-notice.txt).
  - Pretty printer and FORMAT (`pprint.lsp`, `format.lsp`): names such as
    `pretty-stream`, `pprint-logical-block` and `format-directive` are in the
    binary. The files say they are from CMU Common Lisp and "placed in the public
    domain".
  - `contrib/ecl-cdb/` (copyright 2011 Juan Jose Garcia-Ripoll): `libecl.so`
    contains its `ecl-cdb::*` functions and the file names `ECL-CDB.LISP` and
    `ECL-HELP.LISP`. The files' header says "GNU Library General Public License
    ... version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version"
    ([`LICENSES/LGPL-2.0-or-later.txt`](LICENSES/LGPL-2.0-or-later.txt)).
  - Other `contrib/` directories of ECL 26.3.27 (for example `asdf`, `sockets`
    and `deflate`): no names from them were found in `libecl.so`.
- GMP: `libecl.so` exports GMP's `__gmpz_*` and `__gmpn_*` functions, including
  internals that only exist in the GMP 4 series (for example `__gmpn_kara_mul_n`),
  and contains the string `4.2.1`. ECL 26.3.27 bundles GMP 4.2.1 in `src/gmp`
  (`PACKAGE_STRING='GNU MP 4.2.1'`), whose files state the GNU LGPL "version 2.1
  of the License, or (at your option) any later version". Copyright: Free
  Software Foundation, Inc.
- Garbage collector: `libecl.so` contains Boehm-GC banners ("Copyright 1988, 1989
  Hans-J. Boehm and Alan J. Demers", "Copyright (c) 2008-2021 Ivan Maidanski",
  and others) and exports `GC_*` functions. ECL 26.3.27 bundles version 8.2.8 in
  `src/bdwgc`. The README and `include/gc.h` of bdwgc v8.2.8 give the "THIS MATERIAL IS PROVIDED AS IS ...
  Permission is hereby granted to use or copy this program for any purpose,
  provided the above notices are retained on all copies ..." terms, which are
  the text of SPDX `Boehm-GC`. The copyright lines in `gc.h` are: Hans-J. Boehm
  and Alan J. Demers (1988, 1989); Xerox Corporation (1991-1995); Silicon
  Graphics (1996-1999); Hewlett-Packard (1999, 2000-2011); Free Software
  Foundation (2007); Ivan Maidanski (2009-2020).
- libffi is bundled in ECL's source tree, but no libffi symbols are exported or
  imported by `libecl.so` or `maxima.wasm`, so it is not listed as shipped.
- `libecl.so` also holds character tables generated from the Unicode Character
  Database files `UnicodeData.txt` and `Jamo.txt` (per ECL's `contrib/unicode`
  scripts). ECL's tree states no licence for these tables, and the terms of the
  Unicode data files were not examined here: not determined.

#### gnuplot {#gnuplot}

- Not served since the switch to `runtime-v2`: that release and later ones are built without
  plotting (`libgnuplot.so` and `maxima-plot.fas` are omitted). The licence text
  [`LICENSES/gnuplot.txt`](LICENSES/gnuplot.txt) stays for older preview copies,
  which still serve the earlier deployed build; the
  [previous version of this page](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima/blob/64d02c43d839ac6e8f9fb686b7c618f8a292901f/site/licenses.qmd#gnuplot)
  has the notes on that build.

#### Emscripten {#emscripten}

- `maxima.js` is Emscripten's generated JavaScript glue. It has no licence header.
  Emscripten's `LICENSE` offers MIT or the University of Illinois/NCSA licence;
  it was read at the `main` branch (`45a6cffdbdf003665c7f48072191ce5a860fd0f4`).
  The release's source manifest records the toolchain actually used
  (Emscripten and emsdk 4.0.10); its `LICENSE` is in the release's sources. `maxima.wasm`
  contains paths such as `/emsdk/emscripten/system/lib/libcxxabi/src/`,
  `/emsdk/emscripten/system/lib/compiler-rt/lib/builtins/` and
  `/emsdk/emscripten/system/lib/html5/` (observed in the earlier deployed build).
- `musl` is "licensed under the following standard MIT license"; its `COPYRIGHT`
  file also lists parts under other terms (for example the DES `crypt` code, which is under a BSD licence). The Emscripten tree's LLVM libraries say "Apache License
  v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions"; the libc++ file also describes a dual MIT and
  University of Illinois licence for older parts. Which of these parts are
  in the shipped binaries was not examined.

## STACK

STACK is developed at <https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack>. This site
uses it at commit
[`33383047af39c204bf4442802a058f8b918b2b1b`](https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/tree/33383047af39c204bf4442802a058f8b918b2b1b)
(16 October 2026). The earlier milestone-one material, the sample question exports
described below, comes from commit
[`10d323311b7f39fb7b092dd10ce75f7d8632f525`](https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/tree/10d323311b7f39fb7b092dd10ce75f7d8632f525).

STACK's own statement, at that commit: its
[`doc/en/About/License.md`](https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/blob/33383047af39c204bf4442802a058f8b918b2b1b/doc/en/About/License.md)
says the source code is "Licensed under the GNU General Public, License Version 3"
and links to `COPYING.txt`, which is only the text of the GNU GPL version 3 (the
standard text, which has no "or later" grant of its own;
[GPL-3.0 text](LICENSES/GPL-3.0-or-later.txt)). Neither file grants STACK
under "or any later version" (the phrase occurs in the GPL text itself only in
its section 14 and appendix). The grant appears only in the headers of
individual files: for
example the PHP language file `lang/en/qtype_stack.php`, `corsscripts/stackmplite.js`
("either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version") and
`corsscripts/stackjsxgraph.js` ("GNU GPL v3 or later"). So the project licence is
recorded here as GPL version 3, and "or later" only where a file's header says so. The
sample questions are under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0, except the
HELM materials, which are under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0.

| Component | Files on this site | Version | Licence | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|

#### Notes on STACK {#stack-notes}

- The 77 embedded Maxima files: 38 headers say "GNU General Public License
  version two", 3 carry other notices, and 36 have no header. This differs from
  STACK's `COPYING.txt` and `License.md`, which say version 3. This page
  reproduces both texts ([GPL-2.0 text](LICENSES/GPL-2.0-only.txt),
  [GPL-3.0 text](LICENSES/GPL-3.0-or-later.txt)) and does not decide between them.
- The three files with other notices: `stack_logic.lisp` (copyright 2008-2009
  Alexey Beshenov, [LGPL-2.1-or-later](LICENSES/LGPL-2.1-or-later.txt), as
  written in the file), `to_poly_solve_extra_5.38.1.lisp` (copyright 2008
  Barton Willis, GPL version 2 or later), `fboundp.mac` (copyright 2020 Robert
  Dodier, "GNU General Public License", version not stated).
- `stacktex.lisp` says it uses code by Richard J. Fateman, copyright 1987, from
  Maxima's `mactex-utilities.lisp`, and gives no licence; `trigrat.lisp` has no
  header. Their licence is not determined here.
- STACK's `thirdpartylibs.xml` lists libraries bundled in STACK itself. None of
  those directories is shipped on this site.

## MathJax and native board fonts

The reusable native board documents link shared JSXGraph JavaScript/CSS and
STACK binding modules under `native/boards/assets/`. These resources are
extracted byte for byte from the pinned renderer; original licence headers
remain intact. The table above also describes legacy preview copies, where
those same files remain inlined.

Native board MathJax and its original speech worker, mathmaps and dynamic font
ranges are served locally. The build reuses canonical CTM archive integrity and
font-member/licence checks. It does not patch vendor code or disable speech or
braille. The [bundle manifest](native/boards/mathjax/manifest.json) and
[notices](native/boards/mathjax/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) list the shipped files.

## Code and content by the CTM project

These are not third-party, but they are AGPL-3.0-or-later and are listed so the
text is available: the adapter, engine and measurement code of this repository
(`backend/`, `native/` except the STACK files above, `runtime/`, `jsxgraph/`, the
isolation scripts), and the CTM Assessment components in `site_libs/quarto-contrib/`
(ai-feedback 0.9.0, ctm-checkers 0.6.0, ctm-checkers-stack 0.6.0, ctm-runtime
0.9.0, stack-sympy 0.3.0, and the STACK JSXGraph host `host.js`). Their headers say
AGPL-3.0-or-later ([text](LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-or-later.txt)); some files have no
header. Sources: <https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima>,
<https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy> (`1b1d50f69fc1e7eb39846b497657d72be325f597`),
<https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-checkers> (`c366f175aba6b62caa628bc60f57bb1167fc087b`) and
<https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-libs> (`94687f718fd651fc2857bc5242a64e45c8fd4697`).
The header of `ctm-checkers-stack.js` states that the Python wheel inside it also
holds STACK data under GPL-3.0-or-later, so that wheel is AGPL-3.0-or-later and
GPL-3.0-or-later together.

The example questions served under `maxima/questions/` have a README
(`maxima/questions/README.md` on this site) that gives a licence per path: the
CTM team's example question XML files are CC-BY-SA-4.0, the example checker files
and some converted files AGPL-3.0-or-later. That README covers `maxima/questions/`
only. In `maxima/native-questions/` the files `native-checkers.py`,
`native-collections.xml`, `native-numerical.xml` and `native-rational.xml` carry a
"CC BY-SA 4.0" comment, and `native-binding.xml` and `native-json.xml` carry STACK
metadata `cc-sa-4.0`. Four files carry no licence notice and are covered by no
README: `native-matrix.xml`, `native-matrix-python.xml`, `native-mixed-board.xml`
and `native-python-board.xml`. Their licence is not stated in the files.

## Loaded from elsewhere, not redistributed here

These are fetched by the visitor's browser from other servers when a page runs.
They are not copied to this site, and their licences are not reproduced here.

- Pyodide 0.28.3 and the Python packages it loads, from
  `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.28.3/full/` (used by the CTM Python
  runtime). Project: <https://pyodide.org/>.
- KaTeX 0.16 from `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16/`, referenced by the
  ai-feedback script.
- axe-core, requested from `cdn.skypack.dev` only if Quarto's accessibility
  check is switched on, and Algolia search-insights, referenced by the search
  script.

## What could not be determined

- The exact Maxima commit `813903d33` and ECL commit `e4bdb2e5` are now
  archived in the release's sources, but the per-file licence evidence on this
  page was read at the nearest upstream tag (Maxima) and tag 26.3.27 (ECL) and
  has not yet been re-checked against those archives.
- Which musl, LLVM and Emscripten files of the 4.0.10 toolchain are in the
  binaries.
- The licence of the files without a notice (see the tables), of the
  Unicode tables in ECL, of the SLATEC and QUADPACK originals, and of
  `maxima_thread.js` and `share_files.js`.
- Whether each Maxima core file is GPL version 2 only or "or later".
- The difference between the GPL version in many STACK file headers (2) and in
  STACK's `COPYING.txt` (3), and whether STACK as a whole is "version 3" or
  "version 3 or later": only some file headers say "or later".
- The licence of the four `maxima/native-questions/` files without a notice
  (named above).

Corrections are welcome as issues or pull requests at
<https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima>.
